findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is accepted as unsigned caller-controlled JSON with no session nonce, allowing login-CSRF callbacks to attach an attacker's provider account to a logged-in victim.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Sync refresh requests send only guessable user and app identifiers with no authentication secret, so the credential endpoint cannot distinguish Cal.com from an attacker requesting another user's access token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — Identifying a credential only by userId and appSlug is ambiguous for supported multi-account app installs, so refresh can return a different account's token and execute operations against the wrong external account.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — In the sync branch refreshOAuthTokens returns a Fetch Response rather than Google's Axios response, making res.data undefined and silently leaving every synced Google credential expired.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse wrapper, which is persisted as the credential key and makes the next googleCredentialSchema.parse fail after any successful refresh.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — In the sync branch a Fetch Response is treated and persisted as a HubspotToken, so expiry becomes invalid, no access token is installed, and the caught error silently lets calls continue with the expired token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod property is literally "[object Object]" rather than a catch-all, so sync responses lose expiry fields and receive a fake refresh token, causing repeated refreshes and corrupting persisted credentials.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — findFirst targets an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple accounts for one app, allowing a sync event to overwrite the wrong account's secrets.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — Webhook updates carry no version or idempotency key, so delayed retries or replayed authenticated payloads can overwrite a newer credential with stale revoked tokens.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The newly refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but the connection is constructed from the stale pre-refresh credentialKey, so each client still starts with the expired access token it just replaced.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Injecting the literal `refresh_token` when the sync response omits that field overwrites Office 365's existing refresh token and makes the next refresh invalid.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — The shared endpoint is documented to return a flat access token and expiry, but Lark still requires the provider-specific `{code,data}` envelope and refresh-token fields.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Malformed external webhook bodies throw an uncaught Zod error and return a 500 instead of a stable 4xx JSON response.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, a request with no matching header compares undefined equal to undefined and is accepted, allowing unauthenticated credential replacement whenever sharing is enabled.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — The team branch returns before throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs, so any accepted team member can create a team-owned OAuth credential despite the required admin authorization check.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — The team branch returns before the admin-access check, so that check always receives null and any accepted member can create a team credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The any-typed helper returns a parsed provider token locally but a Fetch Response in sync mode, causing consumers such as HubSpot to treat incompatible values as the same type.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed Zod expressions become literal object keys rather than a catchall, so synchronized token parsing strips expiry and other provider fields.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted JSON crosses directly into the credential store without app-specific shape validation, allowing malformed synchronized keys to fail later inside provider adapters.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every service construction refreshes Salesforce OAuth and writes the credential even when the current token is valid, adding an external round trip and database write to every calendar operation

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — The membership existence check also selects and materializes every team member, so OAuth installation cost grows unboundedly with team size

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Saving the SafeParse result wrapper instead of its data corrupts the Google credential after the first refresh, so subsequent service construction cannot parse it.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response even though Google expects a Gaxios response with `.data` and HubSpot expects a parsed token object, so synced refreshes fail for both integrations.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The connection is built with `credentialKey.access_token` after a new token was fetched, so the current operation still uses the expired token and fails.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint and always refreshes against Salesforce, which fails when shared credentials contain the placeholder refresh token used by this feature.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — The computed Zod keys collapse to a literal object-string key and unknown fields are stripped, so sync responses lose their expiry metadata and credentials remain immediately expired or incomplete.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is not atomic, so concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same user and app.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout or abort signal, allowing a stalled endpoint to hang every dependent calendar or conferencing operation indefinitely.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:35 — Any accepted team member can create a team-wide OAuth credential because the team branch never enforces admin access.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Credential-sync requests send only guessable user IDs and app slugs with no authentication, allowing callers of the sync endpoint to request arbitrary users' access tokens.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, a request with the header absent passes the undefined-to-undefined comparison and can overwrite any user's app credentials.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is reflected from attacker-controlled JSON without a server-generated nonce or session binding, enabling login CSRF that links an attacker's provider account to a victim.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Add sync-mode adapter tests using an actual Fetch Response, because Google and HubSpot consume the helper result as provider-specific objects and therefore cannot refresh through the new endpoint.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Add a sync-response test without refresh_token, because the helper injects a literal placeholder that Office 365 persists over the user's usable refresh token.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Add a refresh persistence assertion against the credential schema, because this path stores the SafeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed token data.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — Add a client-construction test after refresh, because the database receives the new access token while jsforce is still initialized with the stale credential token.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Add configuration-edge coverage for a missing webhook secret, because an absent header equals an unset secret and lets an unauthenticated request pass authorization.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is accepted as unsigned caller-controlled JSON with no session nonce, allowing login-CSRF callbacks to attach an attacker's provider account to a logged-in victim.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows file renames from packages/app-store/_utils/decodeOAuthState.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts with import path updates. The actual decodeOAuthState function implementation is unchanged - it simply parses the state query parameter as JSON. The finding claims this is a security vulnerability, but this is pre-existing code that was merely moved to a new directory. The diff does not introduce or expose this behavior; it's a file reorganization. Additionally, the OAuth state handling pattern shown is standard for OAuth flows, and the finding doesn't demonstrate how the diff specifically creates or worsens any vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — The team branch only checks accepted membership and bypasses the imported admin-access check, so any ordinary team member can install team-wide OAuth credentials.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that createOAuthAppCredential.ts was only renamed/moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts. The only changes in the file are import path updates (from './decodeOAuthState' to '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' and from './throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam' to '../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam'). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Sync refresh requests send only guessable user and app identifiers with no authentication secret, so the credential endpoint cannot distinguish Cal.com from an attacker requesting another user's access token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the function sends a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There's no authentication header or secret being sent. Meanwhile, the webhook endpoint at app-credential.ts (lines 22-27) validates incoming requests using CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header, but the outgoing refresh request in refreshOAuthTokens.ts doesn't include any such authentication. This means the external credential sync endpoint cannot verify the request is legitimately from Cal.com, creating a security vulnerability where an attacker could potentially request tokens for any user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — Identifying a credential only by userId and appSlug is ambiguous for supported multi-account app installs, so refresh can return a different account's token and execute operations against the wrong external account.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in refreshOAuthTokens.ts. Looking at the diff, the function takes appSlug and userId as parameters and sends them to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. The endpoint receives only calcomUserId and appSlug to identify which credential to refresh. However, Cal.com supports multiple accounts per app per user (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts). The credential table has an 'id' field that uniquely identifies each credential, but this function doesn't pass it. When a user has multiple accounts for the same app, the external endpoint cannot distinguish which specific credential/account to refresh, potentially returning tokens for the wrong account. This is a correctness bug that could cause operations to execute against the wrong external account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — In the sync branch a Fetch Response is treated and persisted as a HubspotToken, so expiry becomes invalid, no access token is installed, and the caught error silently lets calls continue with the expired token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original token creation call. The original code directly assigned the result of hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() to hubspotRefreshToken. Now with refreshOAuthTokens, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT exists, it returns a fetch Response object instead of the HubspotToken. The code at line 177+ then tries to use hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn and hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken, but a Response object doesn't have these properties - it has methods like .json(). This means in the sync branch, the token data won't be properly extracted, leading to invalid credentials being stored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — findFirst targets an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple accounts for one app, allowing a sync event to overwrite the wrong account's secrets.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 62 uses `findFirst` to locate a credential by `userId` and `appId`. If a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), `findFirst` returns an arbitrary one without any deterministic ordering. The subsequent update at line 70 would then overwrite whichever credential was returned, potentially corrupting the wrong account's secrets. This is a real correctness bug in the new webhook endpoint code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — Webhook updates carry no version or idempotency key, so delayed retries or replayed authenticated payloads can overwrite a newer credential with stale revoked tokens.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the webhook endpoint at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts performs credential updates without any idempotency mechanism. Looking at the diff, the handler validates the webhook secret, parses the request body, decrypts keys, and then either updates or creates credentials based on userId and appId. There's no version check, timestamp validation, or idempotency key to prevent replay attacks or out-of-order delivery from overwriting newer credentials with stale ones. This is a legitimate architectural concern for a webhook endpoint handling credential synchronization, though it's not strictly a bug since the code functions as designed - it's a missing safeguard for a real-world scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync branch returns a Fetch Response with no `.data`, so Google refreshes read an undefined token and can never consume the advertised sync response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code calls `refreshOAuthTokens()` which wraps the refresh function. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response directly (line 7-14 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts). When false, it returns the result of `refreshFunction()` which is `fetchTokens.res`. The code then does `const token = res?.data` on line 91. A raw fetch Response object doesn't have a `.data` property - that's a Google API client response structure. So when the sync branch is taken, `res.data` would be undefined, causing `token.access_token` and `token.expiry_date` to fail. This is a real bug in the sync code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sync branch returns a Fetch Response but this caller treats it as a HubSpot token DTO, producing undefined token fields instead of parsing the response body.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of refreshFunction(). The original code expected hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() to return a HubspotToken directly. When the sync branch is taken, it returns a raw fetch Response, not the parsed token DTO. The code then tries to use hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken, hubspotRefreshToken.refreshToken, etc., which would be undefined on a Response object. This is a real type mismatch bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:16 — The computed schema keys do not describe an arbitrary numeric expiry field and Zod strips the endpoint's expiry, so the advertised access-token-plus-expiry response cannot advance stored expiration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys, which evaluates to the literal string 'ZodString' (the toString() of a Zod schema), not a dynamic key pattern. Zod doesn't support arbitrary key matching this way. The minimumTokenResponseSchema will only match objects with literal properties named 'ZodString', not actual expiry fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date'. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, this schema is used instead of the app-specific schema, and it will fail to properly capture expiry information from the OAuth response, causing the stored credentials to lack proper expiration data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Injecting the literal `refresh_token` when the sync response omits that field overwrites Office 365's existing refresh token and makes the next refresh invalid.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same problem as the golden comment - the parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly handles the refresh_token field when it's missing from the OAuth response. Both comments point out that this causes the refresh token to become invalid, breaking subsequent token refreshes. The candidate specifically mentions 'injecting the literal refresh_token' which refers to the hardcoded string issue, and correctly identifies that this 'makes the next refresh invalid' - the same authentication failure concern in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — The shared endpoint is documented to return a flat access token and expiry, but Lark still requires the provider-specific `{code,data}` envelope and refresh-token fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for LarkCalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens() which, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, calls a different endpoint that returns a flat token response. However, the code after the refreshOAuthTokens call still uses `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)` which expects Lark's specific `{code, data}` envelope structure. The refreshOAuthTokens function in refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns the raw response from the credential sync endpoint, but the Lark code expects to parse it with handleLarkError which handles Lark-specific response format. This mismatch would cause parsing errors when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The shared endpoint is documented to return only access token and expiry, but Webex rejects it unless it also reproduces Webex's scope, token type, and refresh-token response schema.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the code wraps the existing fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) either calls the external CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT or falls back to calling the original refreshFunction(). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false or userId is null, it simply calls the original refresh function unchanged. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function is NOT used in the Webex adapter - the code still uses handleWebexResponse() to process the response. The finding claims Webex rejects responses that don't match its schema, but the diff shows the original Webex response handling is preserved when not using credential sharing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Malformed external webhook bodies throw an uncaught Zod error and return a 500 instead of a stable 4xx JSON response.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the Zod schema parse function can throw an uncaught error on invalid payloads, resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 4xx (400) response. Both comments point to the same file, same line area, and same underlying issue - unhandled Zod validation errors causing incorrect HTTP status codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, a request with no matching header compares undefined equal to undefined and is accepted, allowing unauthenticated credential replacement whenever sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 22-26 in app-credential.ts, the code checks `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the check passes and the request is authenticated. This is a security vulnerability - the endpoint would accept unauthenticated requests when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true but CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — The team branch returns before throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs, so any accepted team member can create a team-owned OAuth credential despite the required admin authorization check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows createOAuthAppCredential.ts was renamed/moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts. The finding claims there's a bug where 'the team branch returns before throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs' but the diff doesn't show line 30 or any changes to the control flow logic. This is a hallucination about code that isn't visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync branch returns a fetch Response, but Google reads the result as a Gaxios response and HubSpot reads it as a token object, so synced refreshes fail before yielding usable tokens.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: when the sync branch is enabled, the refreshFunction returns a fetch Response, but callers like GoogleCalendarService and HubspotCalendarService expect integration-specific token objects (Gaxios response for Google, token object for HubSpot). Both comments point out this type mismatch will cause runtime failures in the sync-enabled path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys are literal stringified schema-object names rather than an index signature, so real expiry and additional token fields are stripped from every shared refresh response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` which evaluates to the literal string '[object Object]' or similar, not a proper index signature. In Zod, to create an index signature you would use z.record() or similar patterns. The code `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` creates literal property keys from stringified Zod schema objects, not dynamic index signatures. This means the minimumTokenResponseSchema will only match objects with those exact literal property names, not arbitrary expiry fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date'. This is a real bug that would cause token refresh responses to fail validation when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result, so persisting it directly stores {success,data} instead of the Google credential and makes the credential unparsable on the next use.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key },`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `safeParse()` - this returns an object with `{success, data, error}` structure, not the actual parsed data. The code should be using `refreshTokenResponse.data` instead of the whole SafeParseResult object. This would cause the credential to be stored incorrectly and fail on next use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — After fetching and persisting a refreshed Salesforce token, the returned connection is still initialized from the stale pre-refresh credentialKey, so the refresh does not take effect for the current operation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code fetches a new token, parses it with parseRefreshTokenResponse, updates the database with the new token, but then returns a new jsforce.Connection that still uses the original credentialKey values (credentialKey.access_token, credentialKey.refresh_token, credentialKey.instance_url) instead of the newly refreshed accessTokenParsed.data values. This means the refresh operation updates the DB but the returned connection uses stale credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — The team branch returns before the admin-access check, so that check always receives null and any accepted member can create a team credential.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that createOAuthAppCredential.ts was only renamed/moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts. The only changes in the file are import path updates (lines 6-7 changing relative paths). There is no change to the logic at line 59 or any team branch/admin-access check logic. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The any-typed helper returns a parsed provider token locally but a Fetch Response in sync mode, causing consumers such as HubSpot to treat incompatible values as the same type.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts (lines 3-21), when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a fetch Response object directly. When false, it returns the result of refreshFunction(). In HubSpot's CalendarService.ts (lines 176-193), the refreshFunction returns the result of hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() which is a HubspotToken object, not a Response. The code then uses hubspotRefreshToken directly as HubspotToken type. This means in sync mode it would receive a Response object but treat it as HubspotToken, causing type mismatch and runtime errors when accessing properties like .accessToken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed Zod expressions become literal object keys rather than a catchall, so synchronized token parsing strips expiry and other provider fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as object keys. In JavaScript/TypeScript, `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a literal string (the string representation of the Zod schema), not a dynamic key pattern. This means the schema will have literal keys like '[object Object]' rather than acting as a catchall for any string key. The minimumTokenResponseSchema won't properly validate tokens with fields like 'expires_in', 'expiry_date', etc., because those computed expressions don't create dynamic property matchers in Zod - they just become literal string keys. This is a real bug that would cause token parsing to fail or strip important fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result, but this call persists that wrapper as the credential key and breaks subsequent credential parsing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `safeParse()` - a SafeParseReturnType object containing `{success, data, error}`, not the actual parsed data. The code should be using `refreshTokenResponse.data` instead of the whole SafeParseReturnType object. This would store the wrong structure in the database, breaking subsequent credential parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — The freshly fetched token is only written to the database while the returned connection is built from stale credentialKey values, making the new refresh ineffective for the current client.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code fetches a new token, parses it with parseRefreshTokenResponse, updates the database with the new token data, but then returns a new jsforce.Connection using the original credentialKey values (clientId, clientSecret, redirectUri, instanceUrl, accessToken, refreshToken from the original credential). The accessToken used in the connection is from credentialKey, not from the freshly fetched accessTokenParsed.data. This means the connection is built with stale/old credentials even though new ones were fetched and saved to the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted JSON crosses directly into the credential store without app-specific shape validation, allowing malformed synchronized keys to fail later inside provider adapters.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 53-57, the code decrypts the keys with `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` and then directly passes them to `prisma.credential.create/update` without any validation of the decrypted JSON structure. The schema only validates that `keys` is a string before decryption, but after decryption there's no validation that the resulting object matches what the specific app adapter expects. This could cause runtime failures when the credential is later used by provider adapters that expect specific key structures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every service construction refreshes Salesforce OAuth and writes the credential even when the current token is valid, adding an external round trip and database write to every calendar operation

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code adds a token refresh call (lines 75-91) directly in the constructor/initialization path without any check for token expiry. The code fetches new tokens, parses them, and updates the database credential on every service construction. Unlike other services in this diff (like GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) which have `refreshAccessToken` as a separate function called conditionally when tokens expire, the Salesforce implementation unconditionally refreshes tokens. This is a performance bug that adds unnecessary external API calls and database writes on every calendar operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — The membership existence check also selects and materializes every team member, so OAuth installation cost grows unboundedly with team size

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows createOAuthAppCredential.ts was renamed/moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts. Looking at the actual diff content, only import paths were changed (lines 6-7 show import path updates). The file content itself wasn't modified - no new membership check code was added. The finding references line 42 and claims there's a membership existence check that materializes team members, but this behavior is not introduced or modified by this diff - it's existing code that was simply relocated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Saving the SafeParse result wrapper instead of its data corrupts the Google credential after the first refresh, so subsequent service construction cannot parse it.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the SafeParseResult object directly (`return refreshTokenResponse`), which includes `success` and `data` properties, not just the parsed data. This means the credential is being saved with the wrapper object `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of just the credential data. On subsequent reads, googleCredentialSchema.parse() would fail because the structure is wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response even though Google expects a Gaxios response with `.data` and HubSpot expects a parsed token object, so synced refreshes fail for both integrations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts (lines 3-21), when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a raw fetch Response object. However, in GoogleCalendarService.ts (lines 83-97), the code expects `res?.data.access_token` and `res?.data.expiry_date` - the Google auth library returns a Gaxios response with a `.data` property, but a raw fetch Response doesn't have this structure. Similarly, HubSpot's CalendarService.ts expects the return value to be directly usable as HubspotToken. The sync branch returns a fetch Response which lacks the expected `.data` property for Google and isn't a parsed token object for HubSpot, causing these integrations to fail when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The connection is built with `credentialKey.access_token` after a new token was fetched, so the current operation still uses the expired token and fails.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code fetches new tokens (lines 72-87), parses them with parseRefreshTokenResponse (line 89), updates the database with the new tokens (lines 95-98), but then creates the jsforce.Connection using the original `credentialKey` object (lines 100-108) which still contains the old/expired access_token. The newly fetched accessTokenParsed.data is only saved to the database but not used for the current connection. This means the current operation will fail with the expired token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint and always refreshes against Salesforce, which fails when shared credentials contain the placeholder refresh token used by this feature.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, lines 72-91 show that Salesforce directly calls fetch() to refresh tokens against 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' without using the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper that other integrations use (like Google Calendar, Hubspot, Office365, Zoom, etc.). The finding correctly identifies that Salesforce bypasses the credential-sync endpoint pattern. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and credentials come from the sync endpoint with a placeholder refresh_token (as shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts line 24-25 which sets refresh_token to 'refresh_token' if missing), the Salesforce code would try to use this placeholder token directly against Salesforce's OAuth endpoint, which would fail. This is a real inconsistency/bug in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — The computed Zod keys collapse to a literal object-string key and unknown fields are stripped, so sync responses lose their expiry metadata and credentials remain immediately expired or incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. In JavaScript, `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a string like '[object Object]' or similar literal string, not a dynamic key pattern. This means the schema won't actually match arbitrary string keys with number values - it creates literal object keys. The minimumTokenResponseSchema will only match `access_token` and these literal string keys, not dynamic properties like `expiry_date` or `expires_in`. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, this broken schema is used instead of the proper app-specific schema, causing expiry metadata to be lost from refresh token responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is not atomic, so concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same user and app.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a find-then-create pattern in app-credential.ts lines 57-85. First it does `prisma.credential.findFirst()` to check if a credential exists, then either updates or creates based on the result. This is indeed a race condition - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same user/app, both could pass the findFirst check (finding no existing credential) and both proceed to create, resulting in duplicate credentials. The code explicitly acknowledges it 'Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential' but doesn't implement any other concurrency protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout or abort signal, allowing a stalled endpoint to hang every dependent calendar or conferencing operation indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens.ts (lines 7-14) that makes a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without any timeout, AbortController, or signal configuration. This is a valid architectural concern - if the external endpoint is slow or unresponsive, it could block calendar/conferencing operations. However, this is not strictly a bug since the code will function correctly under normal conditions; it's a missing robustness feature for a newly introduced external dependency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:35 — Any accepted team member can create a team-wide OAuth credential because the team branch never enforces admin access.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for createOAuthAppCredential.ts, it only shows import path changes (lines 8-9 changing from '../decodeOAuthState' to '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' and similar). The file was renamed/moved but the actual logic wasn't changed in this diff. The finding claims there's a missing admin access check, but the diff shows the file imports 'throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam' from '../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam', suggesting the check exists. The diff doesn't show the actual function implementation where this check would be called, so we cannot verify the claim. The finding appears to be about pre-existing code behavior, not something introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Credential-sync requests send only guessable user IDs and app slugs with no authentication, allowing callers of the sync endpoint to request arbitrary users' access tokens.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the function makes a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There's no authentication header or secret being sent with this outbound request. While the incoming webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) validates CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, the outbound credential sync request to fetch tokens from an external endpoint has no authentication, meaning the external endpoint receives unauthenticated requests containing user IDs. This could allow the sync endpoint to be called by anyone who knows the endpoint URL, potentially exposing user tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, a request with the header absent passes the undefined-to-undefined comparison and can overwrite any user's app credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the code checks: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then undefined !== undefined is false, so the check passes. However, looking more carefully at line 17-19, there's a check `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` which returns 403. APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined in constants.ts as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. So if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy, and the first check would return 403 before reaching the header comparison. This means the finding is incorrect - the vulnerability doesn't exist because the feature is disabled when the secret is unset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is reflected from attacker-controlled JSON without a server-generated nonce or session binding, enabling login CSRF that links an attacker's provider account to a victim.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows encodeOAuthState.ts was only moved from packages/app-store/_utils/encodeOAuthState.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts with only an import path change (from '../types' to '../../types'). The actual OAuth state encoding logic was not modified in this diff - it's a file rename/reorganization. The finding claims a security vulnerability in the OAuth state handling, but the diff doesn't show any changes to the actual state encoding logic that would introduce or expose such a vulnerability. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Add sync-mode adapter tests using an actual Fetch Response, because Google and HubSpot consume the helper result as provider-specific objects and therefore cannot refresh through the new endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts (lines 3-21), when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a fetch Response object from the sync endpoint. However, examining GoogleCalendarService.ts (lines 83-97), the code expects `res?.data.access_token` and `res?.data.expiry_date` - properties that exist on Google's OAuth response object but not on a raw fetch Response. Similarly, HubSpot's CalendarService.ts expects the result to be a HubspotToken object. The finding correctly identifies that these integrations consume provider-specific objects, not fetch Responses, creating a type mismatch when credential sync is enabled. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for the new sync-mode functionality, though it borders on being a bug since the code paths would fail at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Add a sync-response test without refresh_token, because the helper injects a literal placeholder that Office 365 persists over the user's usable refresh token.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real concern in the new parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts code at lines 24-26: when refresh_token is missing from the response, the code sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This is visible in the diff. The concern about Office 365 persisting this placeholder is valid since Office365CalendarService.ts uses parseRefreshTokenResponse and then spreads the result into credentials that get saved to the database. However, this is a request for a test to cover this edge case rather than identifying a definite bug - the behavior may be intentional for credential sync scenarios. The finding is specific, grounded in the diff, and identifies a legitimate testing gap for new nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Add a refresh persistence assertion against the credential schema, because this path stores the SafeParse result wrapper instead of the parsed token data.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the SafeParse result object (containing `success` and `data` properties), not the actual parsed data. This means the code stores the wrapper object `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of just the token data. This is a real bug - the credential update should use `key.data` or the function should return `refreshTokenResponse.data` instead of the whole SafeParse result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — Add a client-construction test after refresh, because the database receives the new access token while jsforce is still initialized with the stale credential token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code refreshes tokens and updates the database (lines 72-89), but then creates a new jsforce.Connection using the original credentialKey values (lines 91-99). The finding correctly identifies that the jsforce connection is initialized with potentially stale credentials after the refresh. However, this is not strictly a bug since the refresh happens before connection creation and the access_token from accessTokenParsed.data is stored. The suggestion for a test is reasonable but the actual behavior may work correctly since the connection is created fresh each time. This is an architectural concern about test coverage for the refresh flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Add configuration-edge coverage for a missing webhook secret, because an absent header equals an unset secret and lets an unauthenticated request pass authorization.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security vulnerability. Looking at lines 22-27 of app-credential.ts, the authorization check compares the request header against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined/empty), and the header is also missing/undefined, the comparison 'undefined !== undefined' would be false, meaning the check passes and allows unauthenticated access. The earlier check for APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (line 17-19) does check for CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET existence, but APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED only checks if both CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET AND CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY are truthy. If the secret is an empty string '', it would be falsy for APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED but the comparison on line 23-24 could still have edge cases. This is a legitimate security concern.
